question: The first railway steamed off in India from Mumbai to Thane in 1853 covering a total distance of
solution:
The correct answer is __**34 km.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **16th April 1853**, the first passenger train ran between **Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane.**
 
• The first railway steamed off in India from **Mumbai to Thane in 1853** covering a total distance of **34 km.**
 
• It was operated by three locomotives, named **Sahib, Sultan, and Sindh**, and had thirteen carriages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The project was undertaken by **Great Indian Peninsula (GIP)** Railway company. The test run was done on **18th November 1852.**
 
• The idea of laying a railway line between Mumbai & Thane and thereafter up to **Kalyan and Bhor Ghat** was conceived by **George Clark in 1843**.
 
• **Sir Jamsetjee Jeejeebhoy, Nana Shankarseth** were the part of the committee and gave concrete shape to the plan.
 
• The fares from Mumbai to Thane in **1853 were Re. 2** and annas 10 for the first class, **Re. 1 and anna 1** for the second class, and annas 5 and 3 pice for the third class.
 
• **10,000 men** worked on the project and **10,000 pounds** had been spent to lay the railway line.
